4 اقترت She (a woman) fumigated herself with aloes-wood. (S, K.) ―
-b2- اقتر النَّارَ He made the fire to smoke. (TA.) ＝
-A2- اقتر على عِيَالِهِ: and اقتر اللّٰه رِزْقَهُ: see 1. ―
-b2- Also اقتر He was, or became, poor, needy, or indigent: (S, K:) or his property became small, though some of it yet remained to him. (TA.) A poet says, “لَكُمْ قِبْصُهُ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَثْرَى وَأَقْتَرَا
” meaning أَتْرَى وَأَقْتَرَ مِنْ بَيْنِ مَنْ [Ye have its multitude of people, of those who have become wealthy and of those who have become poor]. (S.) [Cited voce ثَرَا. See another ex. in a verse cited in art. عى, conj. 4.] ＝
-A3- See also 8.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
